claims.text: Traditional fusion-weld repair is ineffective for the damaged superalloy component because of hot-cracking risk.
Cold spray followed by post-deposition heat treatment or controlled surface peening can restore the component's integrity under aggressive thermal-mechanical conditions.
Keeping cold spray deposition below 0.3Tm maintains a solid-state process.
Particle velocities must exceed a critical threshold to produce bonding.
A low-temperature post-deposition heat treatment enhances interparticle diffusion.
A low-temperature post-deposition heat treatment reduces deposit porosity.
The proposed heat treatment can reduce porosity without compromising the repair microstructure.
The intervention produces a dense repair layer.
The intervention produces a strain-hardened repair layer.
The repair layer has a gradient microstructure that transitions smoothly into the undamaged substrate.
High-velocity particle impacts enable solid-state bonding of superalloy particles.
Cold spray forms a mechanically interlocked deposit.
Cold spray forms metallurgical bonds without melting the deposited material.
Enhanced interparticle bonding and reduced porosity mitigate failure-causing stress concentrations under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads.
The repaired region will have residual stresses closely approximating those of the original component.
The repaired region will have microstructural continuity closely approximating that of the original component.
Cold-spray repair will provide greater fatigue strength than conventional fusion-weld repair.
Cold-spray repair will provide greater thermal stability than conventional fusion-weld repair.
Cold-spray repair will provide greater resistance to cracking than conventional fusion-weld repair.
Localized melting and solidification in fusion-weld repair lead to high hot-cracking susceptibility and compromised residual-stress profiles.

contradictions.description: The intervention presents heat treatment and surface peening as alternatives, but the conditions require heat treatment and the stated mechanism relies on post-deposition diffusion and porosity reduction associated with heat treatment. The peening-only branch therefore lacks consistent conditions and a corresponding mechanism.
